subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Satisficing vs. Maximizing
description: A quick, practical guide to Satisficing vs. Maximizing.

hook.text: She visited 30 apartments and chose none. Her friend visited 3 and was happy. Who decided better?

buildup.text: Herbert Simon coined 'satisficing': choosing the first option that meets your criteria, then stopping.

discovery.text: Maximizers search for the best possible option. Satisficers search for good enough. Satisficers are happier.

twist.text: Schwartz found maximizers earn more money but feel worse about their choices. More options, more regret.

climax.text: Define your minimum criteria before searching. When something meets them, choose it. Stop looking.

punchline.text: Good enough often beats the best.

quiz.question: What did Schwartz find about maximizers?
options: They are always happier with their choices
They earn more but feel worse about decisions
